practices.title: Breathing Tide
practices.desc: Follow a soft, expanding light. Let the next breath arrive gently.
practices.instruction: Let the light grow as you breathe in, and soften as you breathe out. Stay with a comfortable, unforced breath.
practices.safety: No breath holding. The timing is optional: breathe naturally or stop if the pace feels uncomfortable or you feel dizzy.

phases.title: Breathe in
phases.cue: Gently, and only as far as feels comfortable.

phases.title: Breathe out
phases.cue: Gently, and only as far as feels comfortable.

steps: Breathe in
Gently, and only as far as feels comfortable.
Breathe out
Gently, and only as far as feels comfortable.

practices.title: Box Breathing
practices.desc: Follow a steady rhythm, one phase at a time. Holds are optional.
practices.instruction: Follow the light around the square. Each side marks a phase. You can turn holds off and breathe continuously.
practices.safety: Never strain or force a breath hold. Choose “No holds” if holding is uncomfortable. If unsure about breath holds because of a health condition, seek advice from your clinician.

phases.title: Breathe in
phases.cue: Gently, and only as far as feels comfortable.

phases.title: Hold gently
phases.cue: Only if comfortable. No strain, no forcing.

phases.title: Breathe out
phases.cue: Gently, and only as far as feels comfortable.

phases.title: Rest gently
phases.cue: Only if comfortable. No strain, no forcing.

steps: Breathe in
Gently, and only as far as feels comfortable.
Hold gently

practices.title: Here & Now
practices.desc: Reconnect with your surroundings through five simple senses.
practices.instruction: Notice things in your actual surroundings, not just on this screen. Tap a stone for each thing you notice. No writing or sharing needed.
practices.safety: Keep your eyes open if that feels safer. Skip or substitute any sense that is inaccessible, unpleasant, or uncomfortable. Nothing needs to be tasted or touched.

steps.title: See
steps.line: Notice five things you can see.
steps.hint: A color, a shape, the way light meets a surface.

steps.title: Feel
steps.hint: Your feet supported, the chair, your sleeve. No need to touch new objects.

steps.title: Hear
steps.hint: Nearby or far away. If hearing is not accessible, notice three visual details.

steps.title: Smell
steps.line: Notice two neutral or pleasant smells.
steps.hint: If none are available, recall familiar scents or choose two colors instead.

steps.title: Taste
steps.hint: Nothing needs to go in your mouth. Alternatively, name one thing you appreciate.

steps: See
Notice five things you can see. A color, a shape, the way light meets a surface.
Feel
Notice four comfortable physical sensations. Your feet supported, the chair, your sleeve. No need to touch new objects.
Hear
Notice three sounds around you. Nearby or far away. If hearing is not accessible, notice three visual details.
Smell
Notice two neutral or pleasant smells. If none are available, recall familiar scents or choose two colors instead.
Taste
Notice one taste, if comfortable. Nothing needs to go in your mouth. Alternatively, name one thing you appreciate.

practices.title: Soften & Release
practices.desc: Notice gentle tension and release, at your own pace.
practices.instruction: The highlighted area shows where to place your attention. Use only light tension, breathe normally, and notice the release. The final step is rest only.
practices.safety: Avoid tensing painful or injured areas; choose “Relax only” or skip. Stop if you feel pain or discomfort. This is a short PMR-inspired adaptation, not a clinical protocol.

phases.title: Hands
phases.effortCue: Lightly close your hands. Keep breathing normally.
phases.releaseCue: Let your fingers soften. Notice without judging.

phases.title: Shoulders
phases.effortCue: Lift your shoulders just a little. Keep breathing.
phases.releaseCue: Let your shoulders settle. There is no perfect position.

phases.title: Feet
phases.effortCue: Lightly press your feet into the floor. No straining.
phases.releaseCue: Release the effort in your feet and lower legs.

phases.title: Rest & notice
phases.releaseCue: Let your whole body be supported. Breathe naturally.

steps: Hands
Let your fingers soften. Notice without judging.
Shoulders
Let your shoulders settle. There is no perfect position.
Feet
Release the effort in your feet and lower legs.
Rest & notice
Let your whole body be supported. Breathe naturally.

practices.title: The Seated Reset
practices.desc: Ease your shoulders, uncurl your hands, and gently turn your head.
practices.intro: Move a little. Notice a little.
practices.instruction: Sit on a stable, non-wheeled chair, with feet supported. Use a small comfortable range. The figure is a schematic cue, not a posture assessment.
practices.safety: Skip any movement that is unsuitable, painful, or makes you dizzy. Do not force a stretch or roll your neck. Check with a clinician if unsure whether these movements are suitable.

phases.title: Shoulder lift & release
phases.cue: Gently lift your shoulders a little, then let them lower.

phases.title: Open & soften hands
phases.cue: Slowly uncurl your fingers, then let your hands soften.

phases.title: Gentle neck turns
phases.cue: Turn left within a comfortable range, return to center, then right.

steps: Shoulder lift & release
Gently lift your shoulders a little, then let them lower.
Open & soften hands
Slowly uncurl your fingers, then let your hands soften.
Gentle neck turns
Turn left within a comfortable range, return to center, then right.

practices.title: Body Scan Journey
practices.desc: Move attention gently through supported body areas.
steps: Feet & support
Notice contact with the floor or chair. Nothing needs to change.
Legs
Notice whatever is present, or choose to focus on the room instead.
Hands
Notice the weight and temperature of your hands.
Shoulders
Notice support. There is no need to soften on command.
Face
Notice your expression without judging it.
Whole body
Broaden attention, then look around the room.
practices.safety: Skip any area or use external focus if body attention feels uncomfortable.
practices.instruction: Notice contact with the floor or chair. Nothing needs to change.
practices.cardAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker seated in a quiet room

practices.title: Full Muscle Release
practices.desc: Explore light effort and release across several areas.
steps: Hands
Optional: close your hands lightly, then let them open.
Arms
Optional: use a little effort in the arms, then release.
Shoulders
Optional: make a small lift, then return comfortably.
Feet
Optional: press feet lightly into support, then release.
Rest
No effort here. Notice the chair supporting you.
practices.safety: Use only light effort. Avoid painful or injured areas. Relax-only mode is available.
practices.instruction: Optional: close your hands lightly, then let them open.

practices.title: Hand & Finger Reset
practices.desc: A close-up guide to gently opening and resting your hands.
steps: Settle
Rest your forearms comfortably. Keep wrists neutral.
Open gently
Gently uncurl your fingers in a comfortable range.
Return
Return to a relaxed hand. Do not grip tightly.
Rest
Let the hands be supported.
practices.safety: Stop for pain, tingling, or discomfort. This is a movement cue, not treatment.
practices.instruction: Rest your forearms comfortably. Keep wrists neutral.

practices.title: Shoulder Reset
practices.desc: Follow a small lift and a gentle return to rest.
steps: Settle
Sit supported with arms resting comfortably.
Small lift
If comfortable, lift shoulders a little. Keep breathing naturally.
Return
Return gently. Avoid forcing shoulders downward.
Rest
Notice support and stop whenever you prefer.
practices.safety: Use a small comfortable range. Skip painful or injured areas.
practices.instruction: Sit supported with arms resting comfortably.

practices.title: Seated Foot & Ankle Movement
practices.desc: Explore a small up-and-down movement while seated.
steps: Settle
Use a stable chair. Support your leg and foot comfortably.
Small movement
If comfortable, move the ankle gently up and down.
Other side
Repeat on the other side only if suitable.
Rest
Return both feet to comfortable support.
practices.safety: Do not force range. Skip if movement is unsuitable, painful, or causes discomfort.
practices.instruction: Use a stable chair. Support your leg and foot comfortably.

practices.title: Mindful Listening
practices.desc: Notice nearby and distant sounds without recording them.
steps: Arrive
Look around. Choose a comfortable position.
Nearby
Notice a nearby sound, or a nearby visual detail.
Further away
Notice something further away. No need to search hard.
Whole space
Allow attention to include the room as a whole.
practices.safety: Use visual details if hearing is inaccessible or focusing on sound is uncomfortable. No microphone is used.
practices.instruction: Look around. Choose a comfortable position.
practices.cardAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker seated beside a window

practices.title: Three-Minute Pause
practices.desc: Notice, choose an anchor, then broaden awareness.
steps: Notice
Notice how you are arriving: thoughts, feelings, or surroundings.
Anchor
Choose natural breathing, supported feet, or a visual detail.
Broaden
Include the body and room. Choose one useful next step.
practices.safety: Breathing is optional. Keep attention external if that feels more comfortable.
practices.instruction: Notice how you are arriving: thoughts, feelings, or surroundings.
practices.cardAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker resting in a chair

practices.title: Quiet Place Visualization
practices.desc: Explore a gentle imagined scene, with motion optional.
steps: Choose
Choose an ordinary place that feels comfortable enough.
Notice
Notice imagined light, colors, or textures. You can simply view the photograph.
Stay gently
No need to create a vivid image. Keep your eyes open if preferred.
Return
Look around your actual room and notice its support.
practices.safety: Skip imagery if it feels uncomfortable. Choose grounding in your actual surroundings instead.
practices.instruction: Choose an ordinary place that feels comfortable enough.

practices.title: Slow Walking Awareness
practices.desc: A preview of slow steps, followed by screen-away prompts.
steps: Prepare
Choose a clear, level space. Preview while stationary.
Step
Put the screen away before moving. Walk at your own comfortable pace.
Notice
Notice ordinary contact and surroundings, without changing your gait.
Return
Stop in a stable position and return attention to the room.
practices.safety: Use only if walking is suitable. Do not watch or operate the screen while walking. Seated awareness is an alternative.
practices.instruction: Choose a clear, level space. Preview while stationary.

practices.title: Evening Wind-Down
practices.desc: A quiet sequence of support, awareness, and optional release.
steps: Supported rest
Choose a comfortable supported position.
Notice support
Notice the surface supporting you, without trying to sleep.
Gentle release
Let hands and shoulders rest. Tensing is not required.
Set down
Notice one thing that can wait until tomorrow.
Finish
End here or continue resting. There is no outcome to achieve.
practices.safety: This practice does not treat sleep difficulties or guarantee sleep. Stop or adapt if uncomfortable.

resources.label: MINDFUL MOMENT
resources.title: A little pause. A fresh perspective.
resources.desc: A gentle, guided breathing space between appointments.
resources.body: A brief pause is not another thing to achieve. It is a chance to notice how you are arriving in this moment.
steps: Settle into a supported position. Keep your eyes open or softly lower your gaze.
Breathe gently in for four seconds, then out for six. Do not force or hold your breath.
When your attention wanders, return to the feeling of your feet on the ground.
resources.extra: If focusing on your breath is uncomfortable, breathe normally and name five things you can see instead. Stop if you feel dizzy or distressed.

resources.label: PRACTITIONER CARE
resources.title: Caring without carrying it all
resources.desc: A compassionate approach to boundaries and recovery.
resources.body: Caring deeply and protecting your own capacity can coexist. A boundary is not a measure of how much you care; it is a way to make care sustainable.
steps: Notice your early signs of depletion: irritability, emotional distance, or difficulty switching off. These experiences deserve attention, not self-judgment.
Create a closing ritual: finish essential documentation, identify the next safe step, and name what can wait.
Use supervision and peer support. Keep patient information within approved confidential settings.
If distress persists or affects safe practice, seek support from an occupational health service or qualified mental health professional.
resources.extra: Reflection: What is one responsibility you can share, clarify, or set down today?

resources.label: IN YOUR TOOLKIT
resources.title: Finding your feet in the present
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker seated with feet supported
resources.desc: An adaptable sensory grounding exercise for shared practice.
resources.body: Grounding may help some people reconnect with the present. Offer it as an invitation rather than a requirement, and ask what feels accessible and comfortable.
steps: Look around and gently name five things you can see.
Notice four physical sensations, such as the chair supporting you or your feet on the floor.
Listen for three sounds; then notice two neutral or pleasant smells, if comfortable.
Name one thing that feels steady right now. Skip any sense that is inaccessible or uncomfortable.
resources.extra: This practice is optional and is not a treatment or crisis intervention. Stop or adapt it if it increases discomfort.

resources.label: REST & RECOVERY
resources.title: Make room for restorative rest
resources.desc: Small, realistic changes that can support a steadier sleep routine.
resources.body: Rest is personal. Begin with curiosity about routines, responsibilities, symptoms, medication, and the environment rather than assuming there is one perfect schedule.
steps: Choose a realistic, reasonably consistent wake-up time.
Make a small transition between the demands of the day and bedtime.
Discuss the timing of caffeine and other stimulants with an appropriate professional.
For persistent sleep difficulties, consider assessment and evidence-based support such as CBT-I.
resources.extra: Avoid making changes to prescribed medication without consulting the prescriber.

resources.label: REFLECTIVE PRACTICE
resources.title: Leave the day a little lighter
resources.desc: A brief end-of-day reflection without judgment.
resources.body: Reflection is most useful when it creates understanding rather than another standard to meet. You do not need to solve the whole day before you leave it.
steps: Name one moment of connection or meaningful work.
Notice one demand that felt difficult. Describe it without blaming yourself.
Choose one practical support for tomorrow: a pause, a conversation, or a clearer boundary.
resources.extra: Keep personal reflections free of patient names or identifying details.

resources.label: PERSONAL AWARENESS
resources.title: A check-in starts a conversation
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker taking a seated pause
resources.desc: Notice your experience without turning it into a score.
resources.body: A personal check-in captures a moment in your own words. Feelings change with context; no label can describe your whole experience.
steps: Choose the feeling that fits this moment, or skip the check-in.
Add context only if useful. Keep it free of patient names and identifying details.
Decide whether to keep the entry for this visit or save it in your browser.
Use your own words to notice what support or practical change would help.
resources.extra: Serein does not interpret check-ins as a diagnosis, risk assessment, or a measure of professional performance.

resources.label: ASKING FOR SUPPORT
resources.title: Start a useful support conversation
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker seated beside a window
resources.desc: Turn a difficult demand into a clear request.
resources.body: A useful support conversation describes the situation and the help needed. You do not need to wait until you are overwhelmed to ask.
steps: Describe the demand: "I have several time-critical tasks and need help prioritizing."
Explain the practical impact without sharing patient details in this app.
Make one specific request: help with a task, protected time, clarification, or a short conversation.
Agree who will do what, and when you will check back. Use your workplace escalation pathway for immediate safety concerns.
resources.extra: Practice wording: "Can we agree the immediate priorities and who can help?" This is an educational conversation guide.

resources.label: AFTER YOUR SHIFT
resources.title: A gentler transition home
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker standing in a quiet room
resources.desc: Close the workday with a realistic transition.
resources.body: A transition does not need to erase the day. It can help you acknowledge what happened and move into the next part of your life.
steps: Complete essential handover and documentation in your approved workplace system.
Identify one unfinished matter and its agreed next owner or next step.
Choose a small transition: change clothes, have a drink, sit quietly, or take a comfortable walk.
Ask yourself what recovery is realistic today. If the shift remains difficult to process, consider a trusted colleague or professional support.
resources.extra: Original Serein reflection: "A difficult shift does not erase the care you gave."

resources.title: A boundary you can actually say
resources.label: BOUNDARIES
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker looking towards a plant
resources.body: A useful boundary explains your capacity and offers a workable next step. Adapt the words to your role and workplace responsibilities.
steps: Name the request or demand clearly.
Describe your current capacity: "I can complete this after the urgent task, or we can agree another owner."
Offer a realistic option rather than promising work you cannot safely complete.
Confirm priorities with the appropriate supervisor when competing demands affect safe care.
resources.extra: Try: "I want to help. Can we agree what should take priority and what can wait?"

resources.title: Check in with a colleague
resources.label: PEER CONNECTION
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative hands resting on a seated healthcare worker’s lap
resources.desc: Offer connection without pushing for disclosure.
resources.body: A supportive check-in can be short and respectful. Let the colleague choose whether to talk.
steps: Ask permission: "Would a quick check-in be useful?"
Offer a choice: listen, practical help, or a quiet break.
Listen without diagnosing, minimizing, or insisting on details.
Respect privacy and workplace safeguarding responsibilities. Help the person access appropriate support when needed.
resources.extra: Try: "Would you like me to listen, help with something practical, or give you some space?"

resources.title: When everything feels urgent
resources.label: WORKLOAD CLARITY
resources.desc: Turn competing demands into a shared decision.
resources.body: Use a brief conversation to clarify priorities and available help. Clinical urgency belongs within your professional assessment and local protocols.
steps: List the competing tasks in your approved work environment. Do not enter patient information here.
Identify immediate safety concerns and escalate through your workplace process.
Ask the appropriate lead to agree the order and who can help.
Repeat the agreement back and arrange a check-back if circumstances change.
resources.extra: Try: "These tasks overlap. Can we confirm the immediate priorities and available support?"

resources.title: Prepare for a difficult conversation
resources.label: CLEAR COMMUNICATION
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker resting in a chair
resources.desc: Use observations, impact, and a clear request.
resources.body: Preparation can make a conversation more specific. Choose an appropriate private setting and follow your workplace policy.
steps: Describe an observable event rather than a personal label.
Explain the impact on work or your ability to contribute.
Ask an open question and allow the other person to respond.
Agree one practical next step, an owner, and a review time.
resources.extra: Practice: "When the plan changed without a handover, I was unsure of my next task. How can we make the next change clearer?"

resources.title: Notice a small moment of meaning
resources.label: REFLECTION
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare worker taking a step in a quiet room
resources.desc: Reflect without turning the day into a grade.
resources.body: A reflection can acknowledge care, learning, or connection. A difficult day can remain difficult even when something meaningful happened.
steps: Recall one ordinary moment you want to acknowledge.
Name what mattered: kindness, teamwork, asking a question, or noticing a need.
Describe it without patient names or identifying details.
Let it be enough. You do not have to find a positive lesson in every experience.
resources.extra: Prompt: "One moment I want to acknowledge today is..."

resources.title: A supportive team conversation
resources.label: FOR TEAM LEADERS
resources.imageAlt: Illustrative healthcare colleagues discussing practical support
resources.desc: Move from encouragement to practical support.
resources.body: A useful team conversation asks about working conditions and follows through on what can change. This is an educational conversation template.
steps: Ask what is making the work harder and what is already helping.
Clarify practical barriers such as workload, breaks, role clarity, or access to supervision.
Agree one feasible change and an accountable owner.
Check back. Do not ask staff to disclose private health information in a group.
resources.extra: Try: "What would make this shift more workable, and what can we change together?"

reflections.text: You can care deeply without carrying everything alone.
A difficult shift does not erase the care you gave.
You are allowed to ask for support before you reach your limit.
One small pause can make room for the next safe step.
Reflection is a place to understand yourself, not grade yourself.
Some days, recovery begins with doing one thing less.
Your needs belong in the conversation, too.
Rest is part of a sustainable practice.

moments.title: Before my shift
moments.prompt: What is one thing I can prepare, and one support I can ask for?

moments.title: Between tasks
moments.desc: A short pause in a busy day.
moments.prompt: What needs my attention next, and what can safely wait?

moments.title: After a difficult moment
moments.desc: Make space for support and recovery.
moments.prompt: What do I need now: practical help, a colleague, or a quiet pause?

moments.title: After my shift
moments.prompt: What can I hand over, set down, or leave for tomorrow?

sources.title: [1] Calm · Breathe Bubble and adjustable timing ↗ Reference for the familiar expanding-circle interaction, not a basis for clinical claims.
[2] NHS · Breathing exercises for stress ↗ Comfortable, gentle, unforced breathing. Serein’s short timings are optional adaptations, not the NHS routine.
[3] NHS inform · Grounding exercises ↗ The 5–4–3–2–1 sensory sequence, with optional accessibility substitutions here.
[4] Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital · Relaxation techniques ↗ Progressive muscle relaxation background. The shortened routine and relax-only option here are adaptations.
[5] NHS · Sitting exercises ↗ Stable seating and comfortable neck-turning guidance. The combined 90-second seated reset is a Serein adaptation.
[6] Calm · Box breathing ↗ Four-phase square breathing; holds are optional in this interface.

journeys.title: Finding your pause
journeys.description: Explore attention, comfort and a practice that fits your day.

steps.title: Begin with choice
steps.text: A pause is an invitation. Different people prefer different anchors: a room detail, a sound, supported contact, or gentle breathing. Choose what feels suitable today. You can stop, observe, or change focus at any time.
steps.action: Name one focus you would be willing to try. No need to record it.

steps.title: Meet the room
steps.text: Grounding uses details in your actual surroundings. The 5–4–3–2–1 sequence is a structure, not a test. Substitute any sense that is inaccessible or uncomfortable.

steps.title: Explore a comfortable rhythm
steps.text: If breath attention is welcome, explore an optional rhythm without forcing depth or timing. If not, listening offers an outward anchor.

steps.title: Notice without grading
steps.text: A practice may feel helpful, neutral, or uncomfortable. Each response is useful information. Optional session feedback can help you remember preferences; it is not a clinical assessment.
steps.action: Consider what you would keep, adapt, or skip next time.

steps.title: Build a realistic return
steps.text: Choose an available moment and a small action that fits it. A flexible plan can survive a changing shift. Return when useful, without needing to maintain a streak.
steps.action: Complete: When a suitable break is available, I could try…

journeys.title: Working with boundaries
journeys.description: Move from competing demands to a clear support conversation.

steps.title: Notice the working conditions
steps.text: Workload, role clarity, support and break arrangements can affect working life. Individual practices sit alongside practical workplace changes. A support request can make a barrier visible without disclosing private health information.
steps.action: Identify one practical barrier you want to discuss.

steps.title: Separate observation from judgment
steps.text: An observation describes something that happened. A judgment assigns a label. “The plan changed before handover” gives a conversation a more concrete starting point than labeling a colleague.
steps.action: Try rewriting a general complaint as one observable event.

steps.title: Rehearse a boundary
steps.text: A useful boundary names capacity, asks for priorities and offers a feasible next step. Adapt the wording to your responsibilities and local policies.

steps.title: Ask for a specific support
steps.text: Connect the situation, impact and request. Suggest who could agree an action and when to review it. The other person may have information you need; allow space for a response.

steps.title: Close the loop
steps.text: An agreed action needs an owner and review point. If the barrier remains, use the appropriate workplace process to raise it again. This app does not send requests or monitor follow-through.

journeys.title: Leaving the shift
journeys.description: Create a practical, personal transition towards recovery.

steps.title: Confirm responsibility
steps.text: Handover belongs in the approved workplace system. Serein can prompt you to confirm ownership, but it is not a task list for patient care or a clinical record.
steps.action: Consider whether the normal handover and ownership arrangements are complete.

steps.title: Choose an outward pause
steps.text: A brief listening practice offers an anchor in the environment. You can substitute visual details or supported contact if listening is inaccessible or uncomfortable.

steps.title: Allow an ordinary ending
steps.text: You do not have to extract a positive lesson from every shift. You may acknowledge an ordinary effort, choose to say nothing, or ask for support. A difficult experience does not need to be retold here.
steps.action: Choose: a quiet transition, a practical request, or a trusted conversation.

steps.title: Make your transition plan
steps.text: One concrete action can mark the move from work to personal time. Keep it feasible for your shift pattern, responsibilities and available support.

steps.title: Make room for rest
steps.text: A wind-down sequence is one optional way to settle. Your opportunity for rest may depend on working patterns and support. Persistent difficulties deserve a conversation with your usual qualified support.

gentle.title: NHS · Breathing exercises for stress
gentle.scope: Gentle, comfortable breathing. Serein uses optional shorter timings.

grounding.title: NHS inform · Grounding exercises
grounding.scope: Sensory grounding, with optional substitutions in Serein.

release.title: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital · Relaxation techniques
release.scope: Square breathing, muscle relaxation and calming imagery background; Serein uses optional timings and adaptations.

sitting.title: NHS · Sitting exercises
sitting.scope: Stable seating and comfortable movement. Serein illustrations do not prescribe range.

mindful.title: Guy’s and St Thomas’ · Mindfulness exercises
mindful.scope: Background on body awareness and mindfulness; not validation of this app.

sleep.title: NHS · Meditation and sleep
sleep.scope: General wind-down information. Serein does not prescribe a sleep schedule.

who.title: WHO · Guidelines on mental health at work (2022)
who.scope: Workplace interventions, manager training, worker training and individual support.

niosh.title: NIOSH · Impact Wellbeing Guide (2024)
niosh.scope: Six evidence-informed actions for healthcare workplace improvements.

cdc.title: CDC · U.S. Quality of Worklife survey, 2018–2022 (published 2023)
cdc.scope: Historical U.S. workforce survey. Associations are not proof of causation or Serein outcomes.

workforce.title: CDC · Quality of Worklife survey
workforce.limit: Historical, self-reported workforce estimates. They do not measure Serein or establish that an individual tool changes burnout.

whofacts.title: WHO · Mental health at work
whofacts.limit: Global context and modelled annual estimates. They are not a prediction for a person, workplace or app.

sleepdata.title: CDC/NCHS · Data Brief 559
sleepdata.limit: Self-reported population survey. These percentages do not establish that Serein improves sleep.

breathstudy.title: Balban et al. · Cell Reports Medicine
breathstudy.population: Adult volunteers in a remote randomized study
breathstudy.period: Published 2023 · daily practices for one month
breathstudy.limit: These numbers describe a research protocol, not an effect size or a recommendation for you. Serein’s timings and adaptations differ.

niosh.title: NIOSH · Impact Wellbeing Guide
niosh.limit: Six organizational actions in the guide. Serein’s studios are original educational tools and are not those six actions.

burnout.label: reported burnout often or very often

turnover.label: intended to look for another job

workdays.label: working days lost annually to depression and anxiety

cost.label: annual productivity losses linked to depression and anxiety

mentalhealth.label: of working-age adults estimated to have a mental disorder

shortSleep.label: reported less than seven hours of sleep per 24 hours

rested.label: woke well-rested most days or every day

sleepOnset.label: had trouble falling asleep most days or every day

studyMinutes.label: daily session length in the published research

studyMonth.label: intervention period in the published research

nioshActions.label: organizational actions in the NIOSH guide

today: A starting point that connects your current working moment with a suitable pause.
Reduce searching when time and attention are limited.
Before, during or after a shift, once a safe pause is possible.
Choose a working moment, then explore a recommendation or use Help me choose.
Healthcare workers choosing their own support.
practices: A catalogue of optional breathing, grounding, movement, attention and visualization experiences.
Compare options and find an approach that feels suitable.
When you have an appropriate setting and can stop or adapt freely.
Filter by time, focus and movement. Open About this practice before beginning.
People seeking an optional educational pause; suitability remains personal.
guides: A library of short educational readings about care, communication, rest and support.
Understand a situation before choosing a practical response.
When you want a brief explanation or a conversation prompt.
Choose a category, open a guide, and adapt its suggested steps to your own setting.
Healthcare workers and learners; guidance does not replace workplace policies.
studios: Guided tools that turn a workplace concern into words, choices or an editable plan.
Make practical support and workplace changes easier to discuss.
Before a conversation, at handover, or when planning an agreed next step.
Choose a studio, work through its steps, then edit, copy or download the result.
Healthcare workers and team facilitators; use normal workplace decision processes.
journeys: Short sequences that connect understanding, practice, reflection and application.
Build familiarity without deadlines or a fixed daily streak.
When you want a little structure across several visits.
Choose a journey, explore any step, and mark progress when it is useful.
Independent learners, students and healthcare workers.
reflect: A personal space for optional check-ins and words about your own experience.
Notice what matters and identify a possible support or next step.
When reflection feels welcome; leaving an entry blank is also a choice.
Choose a prompt or write freely. Keep patient details out and choose whether to save.
The person using Serein; entries are not monitored or clinically assessed.
space: Your chosen collection of saved practices, routines, reflections and personal observations.
Return to useful tools and control what is stored.
When revisiting a practice or reviewing what you chose to keep.
Use the collection tabs, explore patterns, or manage data and app options.
The person using this browser; local records are not employer reports.
support: Practical routes to prepare a conversation and consider qualified human support.
Connect individual needs with people and working conditions.
When a colleague, lead or professional service could help.
Choose a relevant guide or prepare a clear request through a studio.
Workers seeking support and colleagues offering it respectfully.
finder: A three-choice navigator matching a practice to your moment, time and comfort.
Make a manageable selection without scanning the whole catalogue.
When you know what feels comfortable but are unsure where to start.
Select the moment, available time and preferred focus; compare the explained matches.
Anyone choosing their own practice; matches are preference-based.
checkin: An optional record of a feeling, energy and a little context.
Notice experience and decide whether another support would help.
At a moment you choose; frequent recording is not required.
Choose the nearest feeling, optionally add context, then decide whether to save.
You; this is not screening, diagnosis or live monitoring.
journal: A private-to-this-browser writing space with optional persistence.
Put an experience or a support need into your own words.
When writing feels useful; you do not have to find a positive lesson.
Use a prompt or start freely. Save only if comfortable with browser storage.
You; exclude patient-identifying information and other people’s private details.
quote: Short secular Serein words selected around the working moment.
Offer a brief invitation to notice, rest or ask for support.
When a small reading prompt is welcome.
Save useful words, choose another reflection, or hide them in Preferences.
People who choose to use reflective prompts.
routine: An ordered collection of up to four chosen practices.
Keep a familiar sequence available without repeating the search.
When several short practices fit an available break.
Choose practices, reorder them, and begin each one only when you are ready.
People who prefer a repeatable, adaptable sequence.
saved: Bookmarks for practices, guides and original reflections.
Return quickly to something you chose to keep.
Use the bookmark control; remove it whenever the collection no longer fits.
The person using this browser; bookmarks remain locally stored.
patterns: Counts and charts of check-ins and optional practice feedback you recorded.
Make your own entries easier to explore without turning them into a health grade.
After recording observations, or when reviewing a selected period.
Choose a date range, inspect the counts and denominators, and remove entries if desired.
You; missing entries are unknown, and paired changes do not establish causation.
data: Controls for exporting, restoring and clearing personal Serein records.
Keep control when changing devices, browsers or app editions.
Before moving your records or clearing this browser’s data.
Export a private JSON archive, import it to merge or replace, or clear Serein data.
The owner of these local records; archives are not encrypted.
preferences: Remembered choices for role wording, duration, comfort, text and appearance.
Adapt the interface and suggestions to the way you want to use it.
At setup or whenever your needs change.
Choose options and save. Device reduced-motion preferences are respected.
You; a selected role does not certify that a practice is suitable.
app: Optional device installation, downloaded app content and calendar reminder tools.
Keep chosen resources reachable around your working day.
While online for offline preparation; when a self-chosen reminder would be useful.
Prepare offline content, use your browser’s install option, or import a downloaded calendar reminder.
Users of a supported browser; background push notifications are not sent.
conversation: A temporary draft builder for describing a situation and requesting practical support.
Replace a vague concern with a clearer next step.
Before an appropriate, non-urgent workplace conversation.
Describe the situation, requested support and proposed action; edit before copying.
Workers preparing their own words for a colleague or lead.
transition: A personal prompt for an agreed handover, a transition action and recovery support.
Create a practical boundary between work and the rest of the day.
After responsibilities have been handed over through approved workplace processes.
Confirm ownership in the approved system, then choose one transition and recovery action.
Workers finishing day, night or rotating shifts.
team: A simplified practice view for a voluntary invitation with colleagues.
Keep the shared screen focused on the practice rather than personal records.
During a suitable break with willing participants.
Ask permission, offer adaptations, and use Present. Observing or sitting out is welcome.
A facilitator and willing colleagues; no disclosure or feedback is required.
feedback: An optional helpful, neutral or uncomfortable response with optional settledness ratings.
Remember personal preferences and review your own observations.
After a practice, if you want to record a response.
Choose a response; save explicitly for future insights or leave it visit-only.
You; this does not measure treatment effectiveness.
memory: Remembered timing, visual and comfort settings for a single practice.
Reduce repeated setup while keeping each session adaptable.
When an option suits you well enough to reuse.
Select Remember in the player. Reset a practice’s choices in My patterns.
You; voice stays off until enabled for the current session.
player: A shared space for guidance, optional imagery, pacing and persistent session controls.
Make it straightforward to pause, adapt or stop a practice.
In a safe setting where the activity feels suitable.
Read the practice notes, choose comfort options, then Begin. Use Pause or Exit freely.
People choosing an educational practice; no camera or microphone is used.
playerSettings: Controls for duration, pace, holds, attention focus, movement, sound and visuals.
Keep the experience adjustable instead of requiring one format.
Before starting, or after pausing when changing timing.
Choose only comfortable options; use text or external focus if preferred.
The person doing the practice; some options depend on the selected activity.
evidence: A mapped explanation of the activity, adaptations and relevant background references.
Understand what the source supports and what Serein has adapted.
Before trying an unfamiliar practice or checking a content claim.
Read the scope notes, date, population and linked primary source.
Readers evaluating the educational content; sources do not certify this app.
time: A filter that matches practices to supported durations or a self-paced option.
Avoid opening a timed practice longer than the chosen budget.
When the time available for a pause is limited.
Choose a time chip. Self-paced activities have no required countdown.
Anyone selecting a realistic break length.
style: A filter for breathing, grounding or practices without breath focus.
Offer choice when internal attention or paced breathing is not welcome.
When choosing what feels comfortable today.
Select a style, inspect the matches, and adapt or stop any practice.
Users making their own comfort choices.
setting: A filter for a seated pause or an activity without guided movement.
Match the catalogue to your available space and comfort.
Before choosing a practice in a limited or shared space.
Choose a setting; seated options exclude walking, and still options exclude guided movement.
Users considering their space and suitability.
privacy: A plain explanation of local storage, optional saving, exports and media.
Make storage choices with a clear view of their limits.
Before saving personal words or using a shared browser.
Read the storage notes and use My data to export, delete or clear records.
Anyone using this app; browser storage and exported files are not encrypted.
about: An overview of this educational wellbeing studio and Healthcare Crown Academy.
Clarify the purpose and limits of the product.
When first exploring the app or checking who provides it.
Explore the practices, studios and journeys; use support routes for human help.
Healthcare workers, learners and willing facilitators.

reset: Reorient attention with an optional pause.
Between tasks when a short reset feels useful.
compassion: Recognize that care and personal limits can coexist.
When emotional demands make it harder to identify your own needs.
grounding: Use the actual environment as an attention anchor.
When outward attention feels more welcome than breath or body focus.
sleep: Consider a feasible opportunity for rest and support.
When preparing for rest or reviewing a difficult sleep routine.
reflection: Explore a shift without needing to turn it into a positive lesson.
When personal reflection feels welcome after work.
checkins: Offer a short invitation to connect without demanding disclosure.
When checking in with a willing colleague or yourself.
ask-support: Turn a difficulty into a specific practical request.
Before a conversation with an appropriate colleague, lead or service.
shift-home: Plan one transition action after an agreed handover.
At the end of a shift, including night or rotating work.
boundaries: Make capacity and competing priorities visible.
When a request needs an agreed priority or another owner.
peer-check: Offer a colleague choices about listening or practical help.
When a colleague may welcome a respectful check-in.
priorities: Turn overlapping demands into an explicit shared decision.
When several responsibilities need a lead to agree order or ownership.
difficult-talk: Prepare observations, impact and a clear request.
Before a private, non-urgent conversation using normal workplace processes.
small-win: Acknowledge an ordinary moment of care or learning.
When noticing meaning feels useful rather than compulsory.
manager-support: Connect a team concern to a feasible, accountable change.
When a lead is preparing to listen and follow through.
